title: Ryohin Keikaku (MUJI) moves shareholder benefits back to paper as app and online store stay restricted after unauthorized access
date_note: ITmedia (published 2026-11-24) says the company announced the switch to paper on 17 November and, as of 20 November, could not give a reopening date; the unauthorized access itself was first disclosed on 30 October.
geo_basis: headquarters in Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo, as ITmedia states
summary: ITmedia reports that after unauthorized access, Ryohin Keikaku's MUJI online store remains suspended and the MUJI app is limited to showing the membership card. The company said on 17 November it is sending shareholder benefits as paper instead of electronic coupons while it checks safety and strengthens security. ScanNetSecurity reported on 12 November that the company said a list-type attack on the online store may have allowed unauthorized third-party logins.
plain: After unauthorized access to its systems, MUJI's operator has kept its online store closed and limited its app, so it is giving shareholders paper benefits instead of electronic coupons for now.
exec: A retailer's breach response is still disrupting its online store, app and shareholder benefits weeks after disclosure.
action: As the company states, all users will be asked to change their passwords when the online store reopens; no reopening date has been given.
impact: Online store suspended; app limited to the membership card; shareholder benefits issued on paper.

validation.note: ITmedia relays the company's statements to the press; ScanNetSecurity covers the earlier list-type attack update only. The company's own release was not read.

review.note: date: ITmedia says paper switch announced 17 Nov; date and summary fixed
